$comment: Golden route-generation selections. Area names and polygons are the City of Toronto's 158-neighbourhood file (public/Neighbourhoods - 4326.geojson) - the same names the UI sends to /api/council - so a selection here is exactly what a user can pick. Rings are Douglas-Peucker simplified to <= 90 vertices so the fixture stays reviewable; that is well inside the 800 m walk radius the coverage metric uses. Regenerate only if the City republishes the file.

selections.note: Yonge corridor, due north. The easiest possible case: a straight line already exists.
Bloor corridor, due east. Straight, but perpendicular to the Yonge case.
North up the Humber, then east along Eglinton. One legitimate ~90 degree bend.
Northeast along Eglinton East, then due north to Malvern.
Down the west side of downtown, across the waterfront, back up the east.
South down Islington, east along the lakeshore, north again to Rockcliffe.
Four extremes of the city. No single line can serve these; the point is what gets proposed anyway.
Five midtown areas in no useful order, spread across 12 km east-west.
Dorset Park / Bendale South / Ionview - the mutually adjacent case the investigation saw collapse to a 0.36 km route serving nobody.
Three abutting downtown areas, all within ~1.5 km. Degenerate-by-construction.
Ten areas along Eglinton, west to east. Exceeds the slice(0, 8) cap in buildDataBrief.
Twelve areas along the city's northern edge, Etobicoke to Rouge. Longest possible selection.
